topology_reasoning.device: symmetric two-waveguide evanescent directional coupler with mirrored S-bends
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Two parallel input guides are pulled together by smooth S-bends into a short, narrow-gap coupling region and then pulled apart symmetrically. The centerline trajectories are mirror images about the footprint midline; the black material is the constant-width guide core on layer (1, 0).
topology_reasoning.parametric_strategy: Expose all dimensions as top-level assignments. Generate each arm as a gf.Path centerline from a smooth sampled S-bend profile and extrude a constant-width strip; assemble both arms in one @gf.cell.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive-only recreation using the measured mirrored S-bend profile; wg_width_um=0.65, min_gap_um=0.30, coupling_length_um=9.0, s_bend_rise_um=0.70. The diff was primarily blue edge under-fill (5535 blue pixels versus 157 red), so the next move is a small width increase.
Increased wg_width_um from 0.65 to 0.66. This reduced edge under-fill substantially; the remaining diff was 2699 blue pixels versus 2163 red pixels, motivating a final 0.001 um refinement.

Tried the next valid GDSFactory grid-snapped width, wg_width_um=0.662 (0.661 is invalid because port widths must be even DBUs). This was worse than iteration 2, so the honest best remains wg_width_um=0.66. Added a zero-default delta_length path knob for deterministic geometry-response verification without changing the nominal recreation.
